reason: The hypothesis proposes a specific, untested intervention (controlled aging to induce nanoscale precipitates) on a specific alloy (single-phase fcc FeCoNi) to overcome a known coercivity limitation, which is not directly reported or proposed as future work in any passage. While the mechanism of domain wall pinning is general knowledge and coercivity increase via microstructural features is widely reported, the combination of targeting single-phase fcc FeCoNi with a precipitation strategy to enhance coercivity is a new proposal that goes beyond the existing literature, which either reports soft magnetic properties with nanoprecipitates (P8, P16) or coercivity increases in different systems (P1, P4, P23).
